subject: Quarterly briefing: infra demand surge plan & unit economics
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quarterly briefing: infra demand surge plan & unit economics

Team —

As we prep the QBR slides for demand & cost, I put together an initial demand-surge model and a short set of unit-econ notes attached (demand_surge_model.xlsx / unit_econ_notes.md). The ask here is narrow: we need leadership input on which scenario to use for the executive QBR and two quick decisions so the infra deck can be finalized by next Wednesday.

Key context: a combination of three product events (GenAPI launch in Apr, EmbedPro expansion in May, and Marketplace promotion in Jun) creates a plausible +2.5–4.2x token demand range across our hosted customers in Q2. That drives peak GPU needs in certain regions.

Decision requests:
- Scenario selection (Conservative / Mid / High). I recommend Mid for the exec deck but want your call.
- Acceptable utilization target & fallback policy: proposed 65% avg GPU utilization with regional burst pools and model-fallback to smaller quantized variants when latency SLOs would be breached.

Data points in the attachment: per-GPU cost at current list price, modeled utilization curves, expected token distribution across sequence lengths, and a first-pass estimate of cost delta if we apply 4-bit quantization vs BF16.

Timeline & ask: please reply with (1) scenario pick, (2) any hard constraints (latency, cost-per-token cap), and (3) any stakeholder to loop into procurement/partnerships by EOD Tue. I will incorporate into the QBR deck and run sensitivity sims Rishi requested.

Links: QBR draft folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-infra-demand-surge
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/REDWOOD-12345

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Head of Infra Planning
Redwood Inference

Attachment: demand_surge_model.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: unit_econ_notes.md (notes)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly briefing: infra demand surge plan & unit economics

On Mon, 08 Mar 2027 at 09:12 AM Aditya Rao wrote:
> Team —
> 
> As we prep the QBR slides for demand & cost, I put together an initial demand-surge model and a short set of unit-econ notes attached (demand_surge_model.xlsx / unit_econ_notes.md). The ask here is narrow: we need leadership input on which scenario to use for the executive QBR and two quick decisions so the infra deck can be finalized by next Wednesday.

Thanks for pulling this together, Aditya. High-level: I agree Mid is reasonable for the executive narrative, provided we surface downside guardrails. Two quick asks from my side before we lock:

1) Make the latency SLO impact explicit per-region (us-west, us-east, eu-west). Execs will want a single line that says whether 99.9% latency remains achievable under Mid vs High.
2) Show the marginal cost delta for applying aggressive batching vs a KV-cache hit improvement of +10/20/30% (one-line table).

If those two items are included I support Mid for the deck. Also flag whether any of this requires an SLA exception or expanded reserved capacity purchase — if so we need to surface that as a separate ask.

I'll add a single slide to the leadership section once you update.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Chief Operating Officer
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly briefing: infra demand surge plan & unit economics

Aditya — good start. A couple of technical asks to make the QBR slide actionable for product and finance: 

- Break out cost per p100-equivalent GPU-hour (spot vs reserved vs Dedicated pool amortized) and the end-to-end cost-per-1k-tokens under each scenario. Finance will want a single expected $/1k-token number for the Mid scenario and a sensitivity band.
- Run a short sensitivity sweep: batching batch_size {1,4,8,16} x KV-cache hit {0%,10%,25%,40%} and show latency tail (p95/p99) and cost. This is the single chart that will drive the investment decision.
- For fallback: sketch a canary rollout path where we first route 10% traffic to quantized 4-bit variants and measure quality/regression; if measured regression < 1.5% we ramp to 50% and enable burst pooling.

I attached a quick reference (batching_latency_analysis.pdf) with recent benchmarking numbers from the runtime team; use those as priors for the sensitivity runs.

If you can get the updated numbers by EOD Tue I'll review and prep a short finance note for the Friday sync.

Thanks —
Rishi
VP, Serving Runtime & Reliability

Attachment: batching_latency_analysis.pdf (benchmarking stub)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly briefing: infra demand surge plan & unit economics

Folks —

Thanks for the quick takes. TL;DR below and action items with owners. I'll merge the updated sheets into the QBR draft and circulate the deck Friday morning.

TL;DR:
- Executive scenario: Mid (per Laura) with explicit guardrails by region.
- Utilization target: 65% avg (soft), with defined burst pools for spikes.
- Canary fallback: 10% traffic to 4-bit quantized variant, ramp plan as Rishi outlined.
- Required finance ask: none yet for Mid; if High scenario chosen we surface a reserved-capacity ask.

Action items (owner / due):
- Aditya: run batching x KV-cache sensitivity matrix (batch sizes 1,4,8,16; KV hits 0/10/25/40) + produce cost/$ per 1k tokens for each cell — due Tue EOD (updated spreadsheet attached).
- Monica: confirm procurement lead for possible reserved capacity talks with GCP Marketplace and provide contact by Tue EOD.
- Hannah: produce per-region latency SLO table (p95/p99 vs scenarios) for the deck — due Wed EOD.
- Rishi: I'll incorporate your benchmarking priors; if you have a short note on canary metrics to include, drop it into the Drive.

I updated the Drive folder and QBR draft here: https://docs.example.com/redwood/qbr-deck-draft
I'll attach the sensitivity workbook when the runs finish; preliminary results will be in the updated demand_surge_model.xlsx in the Drive.

Thanks again — appreciate the quick alignment.

Aditya Rao
Head of Infra Planning
Redwood Inference

Attachment: demand_surge_model_updated.xlsx (will be uploaded after runs complete)
